bullets.title: AI capex selloff accelerates: SOX -7%, NDX -2.9% on META/LRCX guidance shock
bullets.body: Thursday was the worst day in months for AI/tech: SOX fell 6.7-7%, Nasdaq -2.9%, with META -7% on a 14C filing signaling hundreds of billions in capital needs and FCF turning negative. LRCX -11-12% on underwhelming guidance reset expectations for peak capex growth. Goldman noted Global Info Tech saw the largest two-week net selling on record at -3.3 standard deviations.

bullets.title: HF de-grossing at historic pace: AI longs unwound, net leverage near 3-year lows
bullets.body: Hedge funds de-grossed 7 of 8 sessions with Oct 22 the 5th largest de-grossing event of the year (-1.6 SD), driven entirely by long selling — largest since September 2025. Info Tech and Semiconductors were the most de-grossed sectors; TMT-focused funds down 9.6% MTD. Fundamental L/S net leverage at 47% (1st percentile 3-year); gross leverage at 312% (96th percentile 5-year).

bullets.title: Rare breadth/price divergence: equal-weight S&P and R2K up even as NDX craters
bullets.body: Thursday marked only the 2nd day since 1999 where breadth exceeded +150 advancers while SPX fell >1%, and only the 3rd session since 1990 where SPY fell 1.1% while RSP rose 0.73%. Hedgeye's rotation from QQQ into RSP (equal-weight S&P) is working; healthcare (XLV) hit all-time highs, up 7.7% in October.

bullets.title: META equity raise of $40B+ reportedly imminent; 2027 cash burn estimated ~$95B
bullets.body: META is reportedly exploring an equity raise of $40B+ within weeks to fund AI capex, with Berkshire cited as a potential buyer. The company's 2027 cash burn is estimated at ~$95B, exceeding cash on hand plus operating cash flow, and the 14C filing signals hundreds of billions in multi-year financing needs. META 30-year bonds are already yielding over 7%.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure ROIC debate intensifies: capex-to-sales ratio must come down
bullets.body: Multiple desks converge on the same thesis: the 'easy' AI infrastructure trade is exhausted as ROIC scrutiny replaces revenue growth as the key metric. Anthropic needs $300B in end-2027 ARR (currently ~$90B) to justify buildout; Mizuho Asia raised global AIDC capex forecasts to $900B/2026 and $1.5T/2027, but 30-50% of estimates are at risk from supply, rates, or monetization failure. The rotation from AI infrastructure builders to AI beneficiaries is underway.

bullets.title: CRWV needs $24-37B in additional debt by YE27; neocloud credit spreads blow out
bullets.body: CoreWeave requires an estimated $24-37B in additional debt to reach 3.3GW capacity by year-end 2027 vs. 1.85GW at YE26. CRWV unsecured bond spreads have widened ~300bps since late August, and the stock is down 30%+ in the past month. Oracle and CRWV CDS 5Y spreads are at their widest levels; neoclouds (MSXXNEO) near one-year lows.

bullets.title: 32 of 35 AI Bubble tickers now in bearish trend; NDX at lowest forward multiple of the year
bullets.body: Hedgeye's AI risk monitor shows 32 of 35 tracked names in Bearish TREND (up from 26 prior week). NDX trades at 20.3x NTM EPS, the lowest forward multiple of the year and -1 SD below the 10-year average. Tech fundamental L/S net leverage is in the 4th percentile near three-year lows, with short leverage at the 99th percentile.

bullets.title: Oil above $100/bbl on Middle East escalation; Brent ~$20 above fair value
bullets.body: WTI crossed $100/bbl and Brent is near $114 on geopolitical risk premium; JPMorgan estimates Brent fair value at $94/bbl, implying a ~$20 risk premium tied to US/Israel escalation risk. Elevated oil is feeding inflation concerns, keeping 2-year yields in a bullish trend and pressuring input-cost-sensitive names across airlines, rails, and staples.

bullets.title: Next week is peak earnings + FOMC: MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN headline; Fed expected to hold
bullets.body: MSFT and GOOGL report on Oct 28 — the same day as the FOMC meeting — with AMZN on Oct 29 and AAPL on Nov 2. Fed-funds futures show ~90% probability of a hold in October but 87-88% odds of a December hike. US PCE, GDP, and personal spending data also print Wednesday. The Nasdaq vs. Russell positioning gap is at +3.4z, the widest ahead of any Mag7 earnings season since 2021.

bullets.title: US flash PMIs strong: manufacturing employment at 2012 highs, but margin squeeze building
bullets.body: October flash manufacturing PMI built on September's 2.0pt gain despite softer new orders; services PMI slipped to 57.9 but new orders hit their highest since early 2022. Manufacturing employment surged to its highest since 2012, but input prices rose faster than output prices, compressing margins. Vendor delivery times lengthened, likely reflecting war-related supply chain disruptions.

bullets.title: XLP staples rotation purely technical, not fundamental; risk/reward now skewed short
bullets.body: XLP outperformed the S&P by 265bps WTD for its 3rd consecutive week of outperformance — the 3rd-best 3-week stretch in 10 years — driven by market rotation not fundamentals. XLP's ERP spread is at the 10th percentile (lowest since 2022 bear market), and its dividend yield (~2.5%) is half that of the 2-year treasury. Multiple desks recommend fading the move via XLP Dec 86/80 put spreads around $0.80.

bullets.title: French sovereign stress at GFC-era levels: OAT yield hits 5%, 24-year high
bullets.body: The French 10-year OAT yield crossed 5% for the first time since 2002; France CDS spreads are up 247% in 2026 and at GFC-era levels, with the OAT-Bund spread near 180bp. The Bloomberg France REIT index is down 18% since its July peak, with 100% of constituents below their 50-day moving averages. ECB is unlikely to activate TPI unless market pressures intensify sharply; a December rate hike is viewed as almost certain.

bullets.title: Eurozone PMI disappoints; Bund yields at 2011 highs amid France contagion
bullets.body: Euro area flash composite PMI fell 1.3pts to 51.9 in October, below the 52.7 consensus, with France particularly weak (-2.7pts to 48.4) due to social unrest. Bund yields are at 3.34%, highest since 2011. JPMorgan's model points to eurozone CPI reaching 4.3% y/y by October vs. September's 3.8%, well above the ECB's 2% target.

bullets.title: UK inflation to peak at 4.6% in 1Q27; BoE November hike assured
bullets.body: JPMorgan revised UK headline CPI to peak at 4.6% in 1Q27 (4.7% in February) driven by energy bill increases in January and April. The BoE November hike is described as assured, with risks of extended tightening into 2Q27 if growth holds. October flash PMI rose to 53.1, consistent with 1.6% annualized GDP growth, but consumer confidence collapsed 11 points to -24.

bullets.title: SpaceX pursuing 80,000 cell tower sites; tower REITs surge, telcos fall
bullets.body: SpaceX is in talks with Crown Castle, American Tower, and Vertical Bridge for access to 80,000 cell sites to build a fourth national wireless carrier. Tower stocks (CCI, SBAC, AMT) jumped 10%+ premarket on the news; AT&T fell 5.3% and Verizon fell 4.7% on the competitive threat. Citi views tower operators as net positive and telcos as net negative from the build.

bullets.title: Global data center capex forecasts escalate: 50GW+ additions expected in 2027, double 2026
bullets.body: Global data center capacity additions are expected to exceed 50GW in 2027, doubling 2026 levels, with 40 of the largest campuses already having 24GW in advanced construction. Mizuho Asia raised AIDC capex forecasts to $900B in 2026, $1.5T in 2027, and $2T in 2028 (24GW/35GW/45GW power). Power delivery timelines and local regulatory pushback are cited as key constraints.

bullets.title: US housing deteriorating sharply: NAHB at 2012 lows, starts -5.2% third straight decline
bullets.body: The NAHB/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index fell to 29 in October, its lowest since 2012. September housing starts fell 5.2% — the third consecutive monthly decline — and pending home sales fell 7.3% to a record low. Higher rates are the primary headwind, with PulteGroup missing on closings and orders.

bullets.title: GS identifies 6-month M&A window before next presidential cycle; 80-name acquisition basket
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs special situations desk refreshed its US M&A acquisition basket with 80 companies ranked by acquisition probability. The thesis assumes deals take ~1 year to close, making buyers prefer to act before the next presidential cycle begins, with the regulatory environment currently favorable for strategic M&A.

bullets.title: Industrial recovery signals intact: TXN flags inflection, Comfort Systems bookings at 2x revenue
bullets.body: Texas Instruments highlighted industrial recovery traction with the industrial cycle inflecting upward. Comfort Systems bookings are running at ~2x revenue, and CAT backlog is expected to grow $4-5B sequentially with >1x book-to-bill maintained. Market rotation is evident in selective buying of rate-sensitive industrial names (CRH, TT, WCC) even as AI infrastructure stocks sold off.

bullets.title: Lam Research guidance underwhelms despite strong demand; semi equipment re-rates lower
bullets.body: LRCX fell 11-12% on its earnings, despite strong underlying demand, as guidance failed to meet peak-capex-growth expectations. The stock's reaction drove broader semiconductor de-rating; LRCX preliminary 2027 WFE guidance above $200B (+30% led by DRAM) was viewed as insufficiently bullish given elevated expectations.
